source:
The Northbridge Library is considering an extension of its evening opening hours as part of a six-week pilot beginning on October 5. Under the proposal, the building would remain open until 9 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays instead of closing at 6 pm. The library has allocated $4,800 to cover additional staffing during the trial.

The proposed change is intended to improve access for residents who cannot visit during normal working hours. However, the pilot would not include Sunday opening, and no decision has been made about continuing the extended schedule after the trial. Existing daytime services would remain available throughout the six weeks.

Staff would record visitor numbers during the additional hours and invite users to complete an optional feedback form. These measures would help the library assess demand, although the responses might not represent residents who do not attend. At the end of the pilot, the library committee would review attendance, staffing costs, and feedback before deciding whether to recommend a permanent change. Approval of the pilot would therefore not guarantee a lasting extension of opening hours.
